gloss: to write in cursive; to write loosely

definitions.gloss: to write in cursive; to write loosely or roughly
definitions.explanation: To write characters in a simplified, flowing style rather than in their standard printed form. Can refer to intentional calligraphic cursive or to careless, hard-to-read handwriting.

examples.japanese: {漢字|かんじ}を{書|か}き{崩|くず}して{書|か}く。
examples.english: To write kanji in cursive style.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{崩|くず}した{字|じ}は{読|よ}みにくい。
examples.english: Loosely written characters are hard to read.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{手紙|てがみ}は{書|か}き{崩|くず}してあって、{何|なに}が{書|か}いてあるか{分|わ}からなかった。
examples.english: My grandfather's letter was written in such a loose hand that I couldn't tell what it said.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{書|か}く (to write) + {崩|くず}す (to break down, to simplify). Literally 'to break down the writing,' meaning to simplify character strokes.

USAGE:
In calligraphy, {書|か}き{崩|くず}す can be a positive term describing artistic cursive ({草書|そうしょ} or {行書|ぎょうしょ} style). In everyday contexts, it often describes handwriting that is too loose or messy to read easily.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {字|じ}を{書|か}き{崩|くず}す (to write characters loosely)
- {書|か}き{崩|くず}した{文字|もじ} (loosely written characters)
- {達筆|たっぴつ}で{書|か}き{崩|くず}してある (written in skilled cursive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {崩|くず}し{字|じ}: cursive characters — the noun form for characters written in simplified style
